senses.gloss:
ITA-5.26.5 caturtha-madaḥ चतुर्थ-मदः
Fourth stage of intoxication
A disorder characterized by some or all the following signs and symptoms: idiocy; being as helpless as a piece of broken wood; loss of the sense of discrimination between right and wrong actions; unable to be roused or respond to stimuli.

ITA-5.6.26 caturthakaviparyayaviṣamajvaraḥ चतुर्थकविपर्ययविषमज्वरः
Intermittent fiver recurring every fourth day when fever persists for two days with one day remission
A disorder characterized by a fever spike on the second and third days: the patient is free of fever at the beginning and end of every four-day period.

ITA-5.6.22 caturthakaviṣamajvaraḥ चतुर्थकविषमज्वरः
Intermittent fever recurring every fourth day
A disorder characterized by a recurrent fever spike every fourth day.

ITA-5.66.29 caturthapaṭalagata-doṣaḥ चतुर्थपटलगत-दोषः
Disorder affecting fourth layer of eye
A disorder characterized by some or all the following signs and symptoms: the ability to see only the stars; ability to see clear and bright objects; complete obstruction of vision in all directions; ability to see the moon and sun; ability to see lightning in the sky; ability to visualize dazzling objects; obstruction of vision.

ITA-2.9.1.9 caturthamāsa-garbhaḥ चतुर्थमासगर्भः
Fourth month of pregnancy
This month is characterized by increasing foetal stabilization, and an increasing excessive heaviness in the body of the pregnant woman; appearance of all body organs and adjuncts; appearance of body parts.

ITA-1.9.3.2.12 caturviṃśati-puruṣaḥ चतुर्विंशति-पुरुषः
Embodied being composed of 24 elements
A body composed of 24 elements, namely: 1. eight primordial entities (ashtaprakriti) including unmanifested microcosm (avyakta), all-pervading intelligence (mahat) and the five rudimentary, undifferentiated elements (tanmatra); and 2. sixteen derivatives (shodashavikriti) comprising the five elements, the five organs of sense, five organs of action, and mind.

ITA-9.6.14 caturviṃśatiyantrakarma चतुर्विंशतियन्त्रकर्म
Twenty-four functions of surgical instruments
A list of the various actions that can be performed using different blunt instruments.

ITA-9.4.38 caturvidhadantajanma चतुर्विधदन्तजन्म
Four types of dentition
Four different types of tooth eruption.

ITA-4.4.22 caturvidhahetuḥ चतुर्विधहेतुः
Four types of etiological factor
There are four types of etiological factors: . proximate cause, distant etiological factor, mild yet potential causative factor and dominant causative factor
